segments.text: Uranus is tipped over on its side. Instead of spinning like a top, it rolls around the Sun like a ball.
segments.headline: It rolls on its side

segments.text: That means wild seasons. Each pole gets about forty-two years of nonstop sunlight, then forty-two years of darkness.
It also holds the record for the coldest planetary atmosphere, at about minus two hundred twenty-four degrees Celsius.

visual.label: coldest atmosphere
visual.sub: Of any planet in the solar system

segments.text: Its blue-green color comes from methane gas, which absorbs red light.
segments.headline: Why it's blue-green

segments.text: Only one spacecraft has ever visited. Voyager two flew past in nineteen eighty-six, and we haven't been back since.
segments.headline: Visited once: 1986

segments.text: Tomorrow, we go even farther. Next stop: Neptune, where the winds blow faster than anywhere else in the solar system. Follow, so you don't miss episode seven.
